business_scope.primary_industry_name: Personal Wealth Analytics and Investment Tracking Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental code system; corporate statute Law 32 of 1927 incorporating Anglo-American company-law features)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States – Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (investment chapter in force 31 October 2012)
Panama – United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty
Panama – Republic of Korea Bilateral Investment Treaty
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements with Mexico, Netherlands, Spain, Republic of Korea, Singapore, United Arab Emirates and Qatar
Tax Information Exchange Agreement with the United States (in force 2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 establishes the national AML/CFT framework and designates the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) as the Panamanian financial intelligence unit. The beneficial-ownership (UBO) disclosure regime is governed by Law 129 of 2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales), as modified by Law 254 of 2021. The corporate regime is governed by Law 32 of 1927 (Sociedades Anónimas). Complementary instruments include Law 41 of 2007 (tax information exchange), Executive Decree No. 363 of 2013 (know-your-client obligations and suspicious-transaction reporting), and UAF/regulatory guidelines applicable to designated non-financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Good Standing and Incumbency of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry or Registrar of the foreign shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; alternatively full consular legalization at the Panamanian Embassy or Consulate for origin countries not party to the Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder General) executed by each UBO and appointed director in favor of the incorporation attorney or resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the notarized instrument; where executed before a Panamanian consul, consular legalization is inherent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the valid passport (biographical page) of each natural-person UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public, civil registry or competent issuing authority of the passport holder's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized authentication in the country of origin plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization where required by the Registro Público or the resident agent's AML policy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence on each UBO, director, secretary and authorized signatory before incorporation. Screening must cover (i) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and the 50% ownership-derivative rule; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases, including Panamanian public officials under Law 23 of 2015; (v) adverse media, insolvency and criminal-record checks at the UBO level; and (vi) country and sector risk matrices published by FATF and the UAF. Results must be time-stamped, evidenced and retained in the AML file. Any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence, re-piercing of ownership structures and escalation to the designated compliance officer (Oficial de Cumplimiento) before the corporate vehicle is filed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Services Portal (Sistema de Servicios en Línea), www.registropublico.gob.pa; corporate name consultation is available through the 'Consulta de Nombres' module and reservation is effected through the 'Reserva de Nombre' service or physically at the Registro Público central office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Articles of incorporation (pacto social) must be drafted in Spanish. The corporate name may employ a foreign word or English expression only when accompanied by a Spanish transliteration or denomination in the body of the articles; the statutory registered name must carry the expression 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.'. Names must be sufficiently distinctive and must not be identical or phonetically or semantically misleading relative to names already inscribed in the Registro Público after the removal of spaces, hyphens, accents and corporate suffixes. Numerals, generic geographic terms and expressions implying regulated activities are administratively constrained.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Bancario (requires prior license from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá)
Financiera / Financiamiento (financial-license implication requiring prior authorization)
Fondo / Mutual Fund / Investment Fund (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores)
Casa de Valores / Valores / Corredor de Valores (securities-activity implication)
Seguros / Reaseguros / Corredor de Seguros (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros)
Nacional / Gobierno / República / Ministerio / Policía (false suggestion of public authority)
Panamá / Canal / Zona Libre (delimited use where it may mislead or conflict with official concessions)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection of a proposed name, the applicant through its registered agent may within 5 business days file (a) a petition for reconsideration (recurso de reposición) or (b) an administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Dirección General of the Registro Público de Panamá. Where rejection is based on similarity with a prior registrant, the applicant may supply a notarized letter of consent from the prior holder or a formal release of the name. If the Registro Público does not resolve the appeal within 30 business days, the applicant may treat the silence as a denial and file a further action before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia de Panamá. The same contested name may not be re-presented during the pending administrative process without a materially distinct identifier.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A statutory registered office is mandatory and the corporation must maintain a resident agent in Panama. For this industry, a non-licensed fintech personal-wealth analytics and portfolio-tracking cloud application, the registered agent's physical office fully satisfies the registered-office requirement. A virtual office is permissible because no on-the-ground staff, server infrastructure or banking/securities license is required; contractually, the registered agent must accept service of process and retain statutory records in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% baseline probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months for a Low_Risk_Standard, license-light software entity. The likelihood escalates to approximately 15% where the company onboards clients linked to shell-company indicators, crypto-asset settlement streams or high-risk jurisdictions, or where the UAF receives a suspicious transaction report; in such cases, Law 23 of 2015 authorizes unannounced inspections by the UAF jointly with other competent authorities with immediate access to registers and records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama General Corporation Law (Ley General de Sociedades, Law 32 of 1927, as amended), Articles 1-3, 7, 24-25, 31, 38, 41.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section (Public Registry of Panama – Commercial Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) / Estatutos Sociales.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required by law. The Articles commonly set an authorized capital of USD 10,000 divided into 100 shares; however, only a nominal subscription is needed and no escrow or blocked deposit is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription of the Corporation’s authorized shares to the initial subscribers, as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, is hereby ratified and accepted. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be and is hereby established at [Registered Office Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and the designation of the registered agent is approved. RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: [President Name] as President, [Secretary Name] as Secretary, and [Resident Agent Name] as Resident Agent, each to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED, that the President and Secretary are empowered to execute all documents, obtain permits, and open bank accounts for the Corporation. FURTHER RESOLVED, that all acts taken prior to this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Estatutos Sociales (Articles) specifying the corporate name, corporate purpose (financial portfolio tracking and software development), authorized capital, officers, director provisions, and resident agent clause. Have the subscribers execute the deed before a Panamanian notary, then obtain the notary's witness certification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises defects, amend the deed by an addendum and re-execute before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of incorporation stamp taxes and official registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá cashier or online payment gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit the official filing fee of approximately USD 350 (covering inscription rights and stamps) through the Registro Público’s electronic services or at the authorized bank assigned by the Registry. Preserve the payment receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a refund or recertification if prepayment is not accepted; re-submit payment under the correct budget code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and registration of the public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized public deed along with the payment receipt through the online e-legal system or physically at the Mercantile Section. The Registry will assign a folio (entry) and conduct the legal review.
required_dossiers: Original public deed with notarial seals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is queried (plazo/conocimiento), respond within the legal term (usually 10 business days) with a corrective affidavit; clarify omissions by submitting an explanatory brief to the Registry Director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Certificate of Registration and certified extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the inscription (ficha) is completed, request a certified copy of the company registration (Certificado de Sociedad Constituida) and a public registry extract to confirm the legal existence and good standing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, submit a written request to expedite and pay priority fees if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold first board meeting and formalize appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors/shareholders of the corporation (private governance, not a state authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a meeting or adopt a written resolution in counterpart. Adopt the first board resolution ratifying issued shares, establishing the registered office, and appointing the President, Secretary and Resident Agent. Record the resolution in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable, obtain a unanimous written consent in lieu of meeting executed by all directors/shareholders.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for cloud-software activities; for physical office locations, the Municipality of Panama (Aviso de Operación) and the Ministry of Health (MINSA) may be involved. No industrial manufacturing license is triggered under ISIC 6201.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license required for software/personal-wealth analytics; optional municipal business license (Aviso de Operación) from the Municipality of Panama.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category III (no EIA required) for digital services/cloud operations; no physical infrastructure.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For the registered office, compliance with Ley 6 de 2018 on integrated waste management and the general standards for treated domestic wastewater; VOCs are not applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification (Inspección de Bomberos) for commercial premises, structural safety review by the Municipal Technical Department, and occupational health registration by MITRADEL (Ministry of Labor) for the office. For fully-virtual operations, only the registered agent office must satisfy these local requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; electronic portal: SEDE (Sistema Electrónico de Declaraciones de Impuestos) at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panama Sociedad Anónima: (1) Execute public deed through a licensed Panamanian attorney and register the company at the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) File the Aviso de Operación (business operation notice) with the DGI through SEDE; (3) Obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and the DGI registration certificate; (4) Elect ITBMS taxpayer obligations and apply for electronic invoice authorization; (5) Appoint a resident agent and fiscal representation with local address; (6) Open a Panamanian bank account. For a non-resident digital service provider supplying SaaS/fintech services to Panama consumers: register remotely with the DGI under Ley 67 de 2022 to obtain a simplified RUC before commencing taxable activities, charge ITBMS at the statutory rate, and appoint a local tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election exists in Panama. Available elections and regimes include: (i) territorial-source income allocation method under Article 711 of the Código Fiscal; (ii) ITBMS group registration (Grupo de Interés Económico) for related taxpayers; (iii) optional Simplified Small-Taxpayer Regime where annual gross receipts do not exceed USD 36,000; (iv) special economic regimes (SEM headquarters, ETE, City of Knowledge) if the entity obtains the relevant license; (v) Remote DGI registration and simplified compliance for non-resident digital service providers under Ley 67 de 2022.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panama VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 0 — No general de minimis ITBMS registration threshold applies: any person engaged in taxable transfers of goods or services, including corporations, must register upon commencement of activity. Non-resident digital service providers must register in Panama before their first B2C digital sale (Ley 67 de 2022) irrespective of turnover. Only small individual taxpayers may optionally elect the Simplified Regime (annual gross receipts ≤ USD 36,000), which is not available to a standard S.A.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Documento Electrónico / Factura Electrónica) through the DGI e-fiscal infrastructure: taxpayers must obtain DGI-authorized invoice ranges, apply digital signature and QR stamping, and transmit XML invoice files (DataInt) to the SEDE platform on a periodic near-real-time basis. Higher-volume and obliged taxpayers must use approved e-invoicing software with API integration to the DGI clearing system. Non-resident digital service providers must issue an accredited electronic invoice for each transactional ITBMS remittance. Failure to use the fiscal clearance channel invalidates input credits and triggers fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Panama zero-rates (0% ITBMS) the export of goods and services. A software-based financial portfolio tracking service qualifies as an exported service where: (i) the recipient is a non-resident entity; (ii) the service is effectively used or consumed abroad; (iii) the consideration is paid by a non-resident; and (iv) the supplier maintains contemporaneous export substantiation. The Panamanian exporter should register in the DGI service-exporter registry and, where applicable, obtain the Certificado de Compra de Servicios al Exterior or equivalent sworn certification. Panama does not impose a statutory FX repatriation deadline (the USD is legal tender and there are no exchange controls); the 180-day benchmark is applied by DGI auditors as the prudent documentary window for receipt of external consideration in the Panamanian banking system, after which a documented justification is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación filed through VUPEA/SIGA)
Commercial Invoice with export-specific reference and zero-rating indication
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical departure (for goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT/MT103 or bank credit advice for services)
Service contract, dated and executed, evidencing foreign use and non-resident beneficiary
Certificate of Exportation of Services (formulario DGI) where required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may reject a zero-rating claim where the export documentation bundle is incomplete, the service is demonstrated to have been effectively consumed in Panama, or consideration is not traceable from abroad. Penalties include: retrospective clawback of all zero-rated ITBMS refunds plus interest on unpaid tax (approximately 10% per annum), fines ranging from 50% to 300% of the evaded tax for deliberate misdeclaration (Código Fiscal Articles 760–762), suspension and revocation of RUC status, and criminal tax fraud prosecution with imprisonment for aggravated falsification of export documents. The review period is extended to up to 10 years where fraud is alleged.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), the national banking regulator and supervisory authority; Panama has no issuing central bank. The financial intelligence unit for AML/CFT supervision is the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized; the balboa is a fiduciary unit at par with the US dollar, but only US dollars circulate in physical form. There are no general exchange controls, no restrictions on current or capital account convertibility, and no profit remittance hurdles. Corporate profits of a Panama S.A. may be freely repatriated and converted without central bank or government approval. The SBP, however, requires banks to enforce internal client due diligence and UAF reporting thresholds on large cross-border movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender regime exists. Panama does not impose mandatory repatriation, holding limits, or conversion ratios on export receipts. A Panama corporation may retain foreign-currency receivables offshore or bring them into Panama without conversion requirements because the local monetary system is already dollar-based and capital is deemed freely mobile.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Panama law recognizes non-bank financial companies and has a fintech innovation sandbox, but an offshore digital EMI without a licensed Panamanian banking relationship is not sufficient for treasury clearing. Local banks generally cannot open nostro accounts to an unlicensed EMI; foreign EMIs may be used only for client-side collections ancillary to the software platform. Full corporate treasury operations require a physical Panamanian bank account and compliance with UAF transaction-reporting rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statute mandates a physical in-person KYC interview for a Panama S.A., and remote onboarding is permissible; however, each bank retains internal policy discretion. Most first-tier banks accept video-verified KYC coupled with notarized or apostilled corporate documents. Beneficial owners must execute a written UBO declaration under Law 23 of 2015. The appointed resident agent (agente residente) must have a physical Panamanian presence and sign the bank mandate, but directors and shareholders generally need not travel to Panama if the onboarding bundle is complete.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner linked to high-risk jurisdiction or PEP status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated passports, apostilled certificate of good standing, regulated financial institution reference letter, source-of-wealth statement, 12-month bank transaction history from the originator, commercial contracts proving the 6201 software business, and a UAF/PEP risk matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of cryptocurrency or unregulated fintech counterparties in the payment chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier showing licensed payment agreements, Stripe and Apple IAP settlement statements, clearance through SWIFT chain with identifiable banks, transaction reconciliation under SBP/UAF AML Circular 4-2018 rules, and audited denial that the entity acts as a money transmitter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low-tax jurisdiction characterisation or perceived opacity of a S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panama RUC tax registration, current BVQ/DGI filings, audited financial statements, details of legal substance in Panama, beneficial ownership register, minutes of board meetings, and invoice-level breakdown of subscription and data analytics revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large unexplained inbound capital injection exceeding the stated paid-in capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital increase minutes, shareholder resolutions, investment agreements, source of funds report, prior bank statements of the transferring institution, and a written rationale confirming lawful economic purpose in the financial portfolio tracking application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee director or classic shell-company red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Disclosure of the resident agent, full UBO declaration, signed powers of attorney, certified copy of the public deed, corporate bylaws (Pacto Social), and proof of operational substance including licenses, insurance, and software platform availability.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses SWIFT MT103 from the investor's or shareholder's regulated bank with narrative clearly identifying 'Capital Contribution', 'Share Subscription', or 'Investment in Software Platform'. Panama has no official FX purpose-code taxonomy; the remittance description and the bank's internal KYC file are decisive. The entity must evidence the commercial rationale, maintain the source-of-funds file under Law 23 of 2015, and report transactions above UAF thresholds. No SBP or DGI pre-approval is required for standard capital inflows.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing uses SWIFT MT103 wires for vendor payments, licensing fees, subcontractor disbursements and foreign payroll. For physical goods or high-value trade, the enterprise may use Commercial Letters of Credit via correspondent banks and standby letters of credit when counterparties demand guarantee. Because clearing is in USD, SWIFT messages are processed through US correspondent banks via CHIPS/Fedwire and into Panama's ACH/CBS settlement systems. Each disbursement must include remittance details consistent with prior transaction history to avoid UAF ex-ante risk alerts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable currency forwards for EUR/USD, JPY/USD and GBP/USD executed through international counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted currencies with SBP-compliant cross-border banks
Cross-currency swaps between USD and other settlement currencies
FX options as prudent hedges for latency in subscription revenues
Interest-rate swaps for floating-to-fixed debt exposure; these are not FX but are permitted under Decree-Law 1 of 1999 when transacted through SMV-licensed broker-dealers

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial taxation system; only Panama-source income is taxable. Qualified taxpayers may benefit from the Panama-Pacifico Special Economic Regime (up to 100% exemption from income tax, dividends tax, and capital gains tax, subject to qualifying criteria), the semilla (seed) and agrofuturo regimes, and the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime with reduced effective rates on qualifying services. Standard deductions for costs, expenses, and depreciation are available. No general patent box or R&D super-deduction applies to ISIC 6201 software activities unless an approved SEM or Panama-Pacifico license is obtained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 701 (Declaración de Rentas / Income Tax Return) filed via Panama's electronic tax portal, Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SFE) and myPanama — Sede Electrónica, operated by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) within the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 701 must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year filers, the deadline is March 31. Fiscal-year entities may file by the last day of the third month following their chosen fiscal year close. Monthly provisional payments (Form 706) and quarterly advance income tax payments are generally due during the tax year, reconciliable in the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rentas gravadas de fuente panameña (total Panama-source gross revenues from software subscription, cloud analytics, and payment-rail fees, excluding foreign-source revenues).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned Panama S.A. must report only Panama-source revenue. Revenue generated from overseas users through overseas servers may be classified as foreign-source and excluded from the tax base; documentary support of the place where services are rendered or where the economic activity is performed should be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rentas exentas o no gravables (exempt or non-taxable revenues, including foreign-source income and income covered by specific territorial exemptions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholder founders, when present, should declare any income from Panama-source activities separately. Foreign-source revenues from financial portfolio tracking subscriptions, if supported by subscription agreements and evidence of the nexus of service delivery abroad, should be listed here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costo de venta y gastos deducibles (costs of goods/services and deductible operating expenses, limited to expenses incurred to obtain or maintain Panama-source income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-resident providers must be supported by withholding tax documentation (Form DGI-05 / retentions) where the expense is a Panama-source expense. Intercompany charges, cloud infrastructure costs, and software development fees must satisfy the arm's length principle and be supported by agreements and invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta neta gravable (net taxable income after deductions and loss carryforwards).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net taxable income should be computed strictly from Panama-source deductions. Losses incurred from foreign-source operations cannot reduce Panama-source income. Carryforward of losses is limited to 5 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto calculado (income tax computed at the statutory 25% rate, with applicable credits such as advance payments and withholding tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should ensure any Panama-source withholding tax credits (e.g., on service fees) are claimed only where permitted under the applicable non-discrimination and tax treaty provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pagos a cuenta y retenciones (estimated payments, provisional payments, and third-party withholding tax credits to be reconciled).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-managed S.A. entities must ensure advance payments are aligned with the provisional return (Form 706) and that third-party withholdings (e.g., DGI retentions on professional fees) are reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto a pagar o saldo a favor (final tax due or credit balance).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the S.A. is nominally owned by a non-resident privacy foundation (PIF) or nominee shareholder, the beneficial owner's identity must still be reflected in DGI beneficial ownership filings. The final tax due must be paid via the DGI portal before the March 31 deadline to avoid interest and surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 701 attracts a penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month or fraction thereof, with an additional 5% for each subsequent month or fraction, up to a maximum of 50% of the tax due. A minimum fine of USD 500 applies if no tax is due but the return is late. Late payment accrues monthly interest at the statutory rate (variable, typically 1.5% per month or fraction) plus a 10% surcharge on unpaid tax. Underreporting or inaccurate returns may trigger fines equivalent to 100%–150% of the omitted tax, plus criminal sanctions for tax fraud under the Código Penal.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Panama imposes a 5% corporate-level complementary dividend tax (Aporte de Ley) applied to retained earnings before dividend distribution, and a 10% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders. Resident corporate shareholders may be exempt if certain conditions are satisfied. The total effective burden on distributed profits is approximately 15% (5% complementary + 10% WHT), assuming profits were subjected to the 25% corporate income tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For dividends sourced from Panama and paid to a non-resident tax resident in a jurisdiction with which Panama has ratified a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the reduced withholding tax rate is applied after submitting: (1) the DGI Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, (2) a completed Form of Application for Tax Treaty Relief (Form DGI-40 / Declaración de Beneficiario Efectivo), (3) evidence of beneficial ownership (including an individual or corporate chain breakdown if requested), and (4) notarized or apostilled legalization of the TRC. Relief must be requested and approved before or at the time of filing the Form 706 retention, absent which the full 10% statutory rate is withheld. Panama's DTA network is limited; the most notable is the Panama–Mexico treaty; no comprehensive US–Panama or UK–Panama DTA is in force.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents for the use of or right to use trademarks, patents, software copyrights, know-how, or industrial designs are subject to a 12.5% statutory withholding tax on the gross amount. Interest paid to non-resident lenders on cross-border loans (including shareholder loans) is subject to a 6% withholding tax on the gross amount, unless an exemption applies for listed debt or certain internationally recognized instruments. Under the limited DTA network, treaty rates may be reduced (e.g., Mexico–Panama: royalties 10%, interest 5%), subject to TRC-based relief and beneficial ownership certification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama does not maintain a traditional OECD-compliant Local File/Master File statutory threshold expressed in local currency. Panamanian TP rules apply to related-party transactions involving Panama-source income, irrespective of size, and the Tax Code requires taxpayers to maintain contemporaneous documentation in compliance with the arm's length principle. The DGI may request TP documentation where cross-border transactions with related parties exceed USD 1,000,000 per annum. In practice, a Master File and Local File should be prepared whenever aggregate related-party revenue exceeds USD 1,000,000 to avoid penalties for non-compliance during audit. Additionally, a TP declaration (Anexo de Precios de Transferencia) must be attached to Form 701 when related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000 (per taxpayer) or USD 200,000 per related party.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price): preferred for technology subscription services when internal or external CUP data exists.
Resale Price Method: applicable when the Panamanian entity acts as a distributor or reseller of software assets/services.
Cost Plus Method: suitable for routine cloud support and data processing services rendered by the Panama S.A. to foreign affiliates.
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method): acceptable for low-value-added software development or data analytics functions, using an OECD-compliant net margin indicator.
Profit Split Method: appropriate where the Panama entity contributes unique intangible rights (e.g., proprietary analytics algorithms) and assumes significant entrepreneurial risks
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's International Financial Centers Law (Law 254 of 2021 and its implementing regulations) imposes Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) on entities licensed as an International Financial Center (IFC) and on qualifying multinational headquarters (SEM) entities. A plain Panama S.A. (Sociedad Anónima) engaged in ISIC 6201 software/cloud services is not automatically within the ESR scope unless it obtains an IFC license, a SEM license, or operates under Panama-Pacifico. However, to avoid the characterization of a shell or conduit under DTA relief, foreign tax authorities (e.g., IRS, HMRC, or EU Member States) may apply their own economic substance doctrines (e.g., controlled foreign corporation rules and principal purpose tests) to the Panama company. Accordingly, the Panama S.A. should demonstrate substantive operations — physical office, local employees (or genuine externalized management), board minutes, bank accounts, and real decision-making power over the software subscription business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panama-source revenues (e.g., Stripe, Apple IAP, or B2B subscription income generated by businesses physically operating from Panama), false deduction of non-deductible expenses, or submission of materially inaccurate Form 701 declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 296 of the Código Penal and Law 42 of 2007, tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment from 1 to 4 years and fines of up to 50% of the defrauded tax, plus interest and penalties determined by DGI. Civil penalty: up to 150% of the omitted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and/or resident agents who knowingly sign falsified tax returns or who direct the concealment of income face criminal liability as co-perpetrators or abettors; personal fines, travel bans, confiscation of assets, and imprisonment of up to 4 years apply. The corporate veil may be pierced in cases of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Panama S.A. with no office, no bank account, no active business, nominee-only officers/resident agent, and no documentary record of commercial substance, used to facilitate foreign portfolio tracking services with all management occurring abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 254 of 2021, failure to demonstrate economic substance upon DGI or UAF (Financial Analysis Unit) request can result in revocation of the license, administrative fines of up to USD 1,000,000 (for regulated entities), a strike-off of the company from the Registro Público, and the imposition of tax arrears plus 10% late payment surcharge. If the entity is deemed a tax-resident operative activity, territorial-source reclassification of the underlying income and double taxation exposure may arise in the shareholder's home jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and resident agents face administrative sanctions under Law 254, including disqualification as directors or resident agents, personal fines of up to USD 50,000, and in flagrant cases criminal prosecution for fraud if they facilitate a false corporate facade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Acceptance of proceeds from illicit or high-risk activities through the subscription app, failure to conduct Customer Due Diligence (CDD) when onboarding institutional users, or use of the S.A.'s bank accounts and financial portfolio tracking platform to layer funds connected to tax evasion, fraud, or third-party money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT) and Ley 70 de 2019, non-subject professional activities may still be fined for facilitating money laundering. The fine can range from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 per offense, plus asset forfeiture. If the S.A. causes a breach in the payment chain (Stripe or Apple IAP), financial institutions may suspend or terminate merchant services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who knowingly operate the portfolio tracking entity to evade AML controls face criminal liability, including imprisonment of 5 to 10 years, personal fines, confiscation of digital assets, and travel restrictions; the court may pierce the corporate veil to recover misappropriated client funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to attach the Transfer Pricing Declaration (Anexo de Precios de Transferencia) to Form 701 when cross-border related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000 or USD 200,000 per related party; failing to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation; using intercompany fees set significantly below or above arm's length to shift profit offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to 1% of the value of transactions not disclosed, with a minimum penalty of USD 10,000; adjustments to taxable income by the DGI with interest at the statutory rate and a 20% surcharge on the additional tax. The S.A. may also be subject to the 12.5% WHT on deemed royalties if the IP is mispriced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable to the extent they execute or authorize mispriced intercompany contracts; if fraud is established, they incur criminal liability for tax evasion and are subject to co-obligor status for the assessed tax and penalties.
